translation_en: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud narrated to me, from ‘Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning what the people of the slander said about her. Each of them told me part of her account. Some had retained her account better than others and remembered it more firmly. I retained from each man the report he narrated to me from ‘Aishah, and parts of their reports confirmed one another, even though some had retained more than others. They said that ‘Aishah said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended to travel, he drew lots among his wives. Whichever wife’s lot came out, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would take her with him. On one expedition he undertook, he drew lots among us and my lot came out. I went with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, after the veil had been prescribed. I was carried in my howdah and put down in it. We travelled until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished that expedition and was returning. When we had drawn near Madinah on our return, he announced one night that we would set off. I got up when they announced our departure and walked past the army. When I had finished what I needed to do, I returned to my riding place and felt my chest. My necklace, made of beads from Zafar, had broken. I went back to look for it, and searching for it delayed me. The group of men who used to prepare me for travel came and lifted my howdah, placed it on the camel I rode, and set it off, thinking I was inside it. At that time women were light in weight. They had not grown heavy or been covered with flesh; they ate only a little food. So the people did not notice how light the howdah was when they lifted and carried it. I was a young girl. They sent the camel on and continued. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their stopping places, but there was no caller or responder among them. I went to the place where I had been staying and thought that they would notice I was missing and return for me. While I was sitting there, sleep overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. In the morning he reached the place where I was and saw the dark outline of a sleeping person. He recognized me when he saw me, because he had seen me before the veil was prescribed. I woke when he said, ‘We belong to Allah, and to Him we return.’ When he recognized me, I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, we did not exchange a single word, and I heard no word from him except that phrase. He made his camel kneel, pressed its foreleg down, and I got up and mounted it. He then led the camel with me until we reached the army in the heat of midday, while they were stopped to rest. ‘Aishah said: Some people were ruined because of me, and the one who took the leading part in the slander was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. ‘Urwah said: I was informed that the story used to be spread and discussed in his presence, and that he approved of it, listened to it, and sought it out. ‘Urwah also said: Among the people of the slander, only Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh were named to me, along with other people about whom I have no knowledge. They were a group, as Allah Most High said, and the one said to have borne the greatest share of it was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. ‘Urwah said: ‘Aishah disliked having Hassan insulted in her presence. She would say that he was the one who said, “My father, his father, and my honor are a shield for Muhammad’s honor against you.” ‘Aishah said: When we arrived in Madinah, I became ill for a month. People were discussing what the slanderers had said, but I knew nothing about it. What troubled me during my illness was that I no longer received from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only come in, greet me, and say, “How is that one?” Then he would leave. That troubled me, though I did not know of the evil being said, until I had recovered. Then I went out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi‘, our place for relieving ourselves. We used to go out only from one night to the next. This was before we had latrines near our homes. Our practice was like that of the early Arabs in the open country, and we disliked having latrines near our houses. Umm Mistah and I set out. She was the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn ‘Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn ‘Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn ‘Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. When Umm Mistah and I were returning toward my home after finishing what we needed to do, she stumbled over her cloak and said, “May Mistah be ruined!” I said to her, “What a terrible thing to say! Are you insulting a man who was present at Badr?” She said, “You poor woman, have you not heard what he said?” I asked, “What did he say?” Then she told me what the people of the slander had said. ‘Aishah said: My illness grew worse. When I returned home, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted me, and said, “How is that one?” I said, “Will you let me go to my parents?” I wanted to make sure of the report from them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission. I said to my mother, “Mother, what are people talking about?” She said, “My daughter, take it lightly. By Allah, it is rare for a beautiful woman who is loved by a man and has co-wives not to have them speak against her.” I said, “Glory be to Allah! Are people really talking about this?” I cried through that night until morning. My tears would not stop, and I could not sleep. In the morning I was still crying. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation had been delayed, to ask their advice about separating from his wife. Usamah advised him according to what he knew of his family’s innocence and the affection he knew the Prophet held for them. Usamah said, “They are your family, and we know nothing about them except good.” ‘Ali said, “Messenger of Allah, Allah has not placed any restriction on you. There are many women besides her. Ask the servant girl and she will tell you the truth.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for Barirah and said, “Barirah, have you seen anything that makes you doubt her?” Barirah said, “By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I could criticize, except that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while her family’s dough is rising, and then the household animal comes and eats it.” ‘Aishah said: That day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood up on the pulpit and sought support against ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. He said, “Muslims, who will help me against a man whose harm to my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing about my family except good. They have also mentioned a man about whom I know nothing except good, and he never entered my family’s home except when he was with me.” ‘Aishah said: Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh, the brother of Banu ‘Abd al-Ashhal, stood up and said, “Messenger of Allah, I will help you. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; if he is one of our brothers from the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command.” A man from the Khazraj then stood up. Hassan’s mother was his paternal cousin from his branch. It was Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj. ‘Aishah said: He had previously been a righteous man, but tribal zeal overcame him. He said to Sa‘d, “By the life of Allah, you have lied. You will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him. If he were from your own clan, you would not want him killed.” Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was Sa‘d’s cousin, stood up and said to Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, “By the life of Allah, you have lied. We will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.” ‘Aishah said: The two clans, Aws and Khazraj, became stirred up until they were about to fight, while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. He kept calming them until they fell silent, and then he was silent. ‘Aishah said: I cried that whole day, with tears that would not stop and without sleeping. The next morning my parents were with me. I had cried for two nights and a day, with tears that would not stop and without sleeping, until I thought the crying would split my liver. While my parents were sitting with me and I was crying, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to come in. I let her in, and she sat and cried with me. While we were like that, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in, greeted us, and sat down. He had not sat with me since people first said what they said about me. A month had passed without any revelation being sent to him concerning me. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, bore witness, then said, “To continue: ‘Aishah, I have heard such-and-such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare you innocent. If you have committed a sin, ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant admits a sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance.” ‘Aishah said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished speaking, my tears dried up until I could no longer feel a single drop. I said to my father, “Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.” My father said, “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” I said to my mother, “Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.” My mother said, “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.” I said, “I am a young girl and do not recite much of the Quran. By Allah, I know that you have heard this story until it settled in your hearts and you believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me. But if I admit something to you, while Allah knows I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I can find no example for you and me except the father of Yusuf, who said, ‘So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe’ (12:18).” Then I turned over and lay on my bed. Allah knew that I was innocent then, and that Allah would declare me innocent. But by Allah, I did not think Allah would send down revelation about me that would be recited. My situation seemed too insignificant to me for Allah to speak about it. I had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in which Allah declared me innocent. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not left his seat, and no one from the household had gone out, when revelation came down to him. The state that used to overcome him came over him, until sweat like pearls ran down from him, even on a cold day, because of the weight of the words revealed to him. When that state passed from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling. The first words he said were, “Aishah, Allah has declared you innocent.” My mother said to me, “Get up and go to him.” I said, “By Allah, I will not get up to go to him. I will praise none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.” ‘Aishah said: Allah Most High revealed the ten verses beginning, “Indeed, those who brought the slander,” concerning my innocence (24:11–22). Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who used to support Mistah ibn Uthathah because of their kinship and his poverty, said, “By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah again after what he said about ‘Aishah.” Then Allah revealed, “Those of you who possess grace and abundance should not swear…” up to the words, “…All-Forgiving, Most Merciful” (24:22). Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said, “Indeed, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me.” So he resumed the support he had been giving Mistah and said, “By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him.” ‘Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about me. He said to Zaynab, “What have you known or seen?” She said, “Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing about her except good.” ‘Aishah said: She was the one among the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who used to compete with me for his favor, but Allah protected her through her piety. Her sister Hamnah began defending her, and she was among those who perished. Ibn Shihab said: This is what reached me from the reports of these men. Then ‘Urwah said: ‘Aishah said, “By Allah, the man about whom people said what they said would say, ‘Glory be to Allah! By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I have never uncovered any woman’s covering.’” ‘Aishah said: He was later killed in the cause of Allah.
